### 2 Atoms, molecules and stoichiometry - Multiple Choice: Easy

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-easy-q1 data-answer="B"}
### Question 1 · Relative atomic mass

What is meant by the relative atomic mass of an element?

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>The mass of one atom compared with the mass of one electron</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>The weighted mean mass of an atom compared with $\frac{1}{12}$ of the mass of a carbon-12 atom</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>The mass of one hydrogen atom compared with one carbon atom</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>The mass of one proton compared with one neutron</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> Relative atomic mass is a weighted mean because naturally occurring elements may contain several isotopes.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-easy-q2 data-answer="A"}
### Question 2 · Isotopes

Which statement correctly describes two isotopes of the same element?

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>They have different numbers of protons but the same number of neutrons.</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>They have different numbers of protons and different chemical properties.</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>They have the same mass number and different atomic numbers.</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Isotopes have the same proton number, so they are the same element, but different neutron numbers.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-easy-q3 data-answer="C"}
### Question 3 · Relative formula mass

What is the relative formula mass of $(\ce{NH4})2\ce{SO4}$? Use $A_r$: N = 14.0, H = 1.0, S = 32.1 and O = 16.0.

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>98.1</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>98.0</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>132.1</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>132.0</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> $M_r=(2\times14.0)+(8\times1.0)+32.1+(4\times16.0)=132.1$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-easy-q4 data-answer="D"}
### Question 4 · Weighted isotope abundance

An element contains 91.75% of an isotope with mass 55.0 and 8.25% of an isotope with mass 56.0. What is its relative atomic mass?

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>55.000</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>55.500</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>56.000</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>55.083</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> $A_r=(55.0\times0.9175)+(56.0\times0.0825)=55.0825$, which rounds to 55.083.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-easy-q5 data-answer="D"}
### Question 5 · Avogadro constant

What is the number of molecules in $500\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of oxygen gas at RTP? Take the molar gas volume as $24.0\ \mathrm{dm^3\ mol^{-1}}$.

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$3.00\times10^{23}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$3.00\times10^{26}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$1.25\times10^{21}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$1.25\times10^{22}$</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> $500\ \mathrm{cm^3}=0.500\ \mathrm{dm^3}$, so $n=0.500/24.0=0.0208\ \mathrm{mol}$ and $N=0.0208\times6.02\times10^{23}=1.25\times10^{22}$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-easy-q6 data-answer="A"}
### Question 6 · Balancing equations

Which set of coefficients balances the equation?

$$\ce{Mg3N2 + H2O -> Mg(OH)2 + NH3}$$

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$1,6,3,2$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$1,3,3,2$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$2,6,3,4$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$1,4,3,2$</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Three magnesium atoms require $3\ce{Mg(OH)2}$; two nitrogen atoms give $2\ce{NH3}$, requiring six water molecules.</p></details>
:::

### 2 Atoms, molecules and stoichiometry - Multiple Choice: Medium

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-medium-q1 data-answer="C"}
### Question 1 · Hydrated salts

A hydrated carbonate has formula $\ce{X2CO3.10H2O}$ and relative formula mass 286. What is element X? Use $A_r$: C = 12.0, O = 16.0 and H = 1.0.

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Li</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>K</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>Na</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Rb</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> The anhydrous part contributes $12+48=60$ and the water contributes $180$, so $2A_r(X)=286-240=46$ and $A_r(X)=23$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-medium-q2 data-answer="C"}
### Question 2 · Gas stoichiometry

Nitrogen reacts with excess hydrogen. $2.00\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ of nitrogen is available at standard conditions and 15.0% reacts. What mass of ammonia forms? Use a molar gas volume of $22.4\ \mathrm{dm^3\ mol^{-1}}$ for this question.

$$\ce{N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3}$$

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$2.83\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$1.42\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$0.455\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$0.213\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Reacted nitrogen is $2.00\times0.150/22.4=0.0134\ \mathrm{mol}$; ammonia is $0.0268\ \mathrm{mol}$, giving approximately $0.455\ \mathrm{g}$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-medium-q3 data-answer="B"}
### Question 3 · Reacting amounts

Chlorine reacts with cold aqueous sodium hydroxide:

$$\ce{Cl2 + 2NaOH -> NaCl + NaOCl + H2O}$$

What mass of $\ce{NaOCl}$ forms from $0.125\ \mathrm{mol}$ of $\ce{Cl2}$ with excess $\ce{NaOH}$? Use $M_r(\ce{NaOCl})=74.5$.

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$13.3\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$9.31\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$18.6\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$26.6\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> The mole ratio is $1:1$, so $n(\ce{NaOCl})=0.125$ and mass $=0.125\times74.5=9.31\ \mathrm{g}$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-medium-q4 data-answer="A"}
### Question 4 · Thermal decomposition

When $7.40\ \mathrm{g}$ of $\ce{Mg(NO3)2}$ is heated, what mass of nitrogen dioxide forms? Use $M_r(\ce{Mg(NO3)2})=148$.

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$4.60\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$1.50\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$2.30\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$3.00\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> $7.40/148=0.0500\ \mathrm{mol}$ of salt forms $0.100\ \mathrm{mol}$ of $\ce{NO2}$, so the mass is $0.100\times46.0=4.60\ \mathrm{g}$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-medium-q5 data-answer="D"}
### Question 5 · Empirical formula from a gas

A $0.144\ \mathrm{g}$ aluminium compound burns to form $72.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $\ce{CO2}$ at RTP. Which is its formula? Use $A_r(\ce{Al})=27.0$.

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$\ce{Al2C3}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$\ce{Al3C4}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$\ce{Al5C3}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$\ce{Al4C3}$</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> $n(\ce{CO2})=0.0720/24.0=0.00300\ \mathrm{mol}$, so the sample contains $0.00300\ \mathrm{mol}$ C. The aluminium-to-carbon ratio is $0.00533:0.00300\approx4:3$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-medium-q6 data-answer="D"}
### Question 6 · Limiting reagent

What metal reacts completely with $1.15\ \mathrm{g}$ of metal and $300\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of oxygen at RTP to form an oxide containing $\ce{O^{2-}}$? Choose from Ca, Na, K and Mg.

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>Ca</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>Na</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>K</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>Mg</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> $n(\ce{O2})=0.300/24.0=0.0125\ \mathrm{mol}$. For magnesium, $1.15/24.3=0.0473\ \mathrm{mol}$ and the required oxygen is $0.0237\ \mathrm{mol}$, so oxygen is available in the expected limiting ratio.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-medium-q7 data-answer="D"}
### Question 7 · Particles in a sample

A coin has mass $10.0\ \mathrm{g}$ and contains 20.0% nickel by mass. How many nickel atoms are present? Use $A_r(\ce{Ni})=58.7$.

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$4.30\times10^{22}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$1.03\times10^{23}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$1.20\times10^{24}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$2.05\times10^{22}$</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> Nickel mass is $2.00\ \mathrm{g}$, so $n=2.00/58.7=0.0341\ \mathrm{mol}$ and $N=2.05\times10^{22}$ atoms.</p></details>
:::

### 2 Atoms, molecules and stoichiometry - Multiple Choice: Hard

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-hard-q1 data-answer="D"}
### Question 1 · Combustion and gas absorption

Carbon is burned in a limited amount of oxygen. Half the carbon forms $\ce{CO2}$ and half forms $\ce{CO}$. The carbon oxides are passed through excess aqueous sodium hydroxide. Which gas volume remains if the starting carbon sample is $1.00\ \mathrm{g}$ and the gas volume is measured at RTP?

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$3.00\ \mathrm{dm^3}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$2.00\ \mathrm{dm^3}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$1.50\ \mathrm{dm^3}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$1.00\ \mathrm{dm^3}$</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>D.</strong> The amount of carbon monoxide is $0.5/12.0=0.0417\ \mathrm{mol}$, so the remaining gas volume is $0.0417\times24.0=1.00\ \mathrm{dm^3}$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-hard-q2 data-answer="C"}
### Question 2 · Neutralisation of carbonate

An eggshell is 5.0% $\ce{CaCO3}$ by mass. Each egg contains a $50.0\ \mathrm{g}$ shell, and the carbonate in the shell neutralises $50.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $2.00\ \mathrm{mol\ dm^{-3}}$ ethanoic acid. How many eggshells are needed?

$$\ce{CaCO3 + 2CH3COOH -> Ca(CH3COO)2 + H2O + CO2}$$

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>4</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>3</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>2</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>1</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> Acid amount is $0.0500\times2.00=0.100\ \mathrm{mol}$, requiring $0.0500\ \mathrm{mol}$ carbonate, or $5.00\ \mathrm{g}$. Each shell contains $2.50\ \mathrm{g}$, so two shells are required.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-hard-q3 data-answer="C"}
### Question 3 · Titration of a basic oxide

An oxide sample is dissolved in $250\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of solution. A $25.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ portion requires $15.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $2.00\ \mathrm{mol\ dm^{-3}}$ sulfuric acid. If the oxide is $\ce{K2O}$, what mass was present?

$$\ce{K2O + H2SO4 -> K2SO4 + H2O}$$

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$56.6\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$47.1\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$28.3\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$2.83\ \mathrm{g}$</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> The aliquot contains $0.0150\times2.00=0.0300\ \mathrm{mol}$ acid; the whole solution contains $0.300\ \mathrm{mol}$, hence $0.300\ \mathrm{mol}$ $\ce{K2O}$ and mass $0.300\times94.2=28.3\ \mathrm{g}$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-hard-q4 data-answer="A"}
### Question 4 · Redox titration

In a ferrochrome sample, $1.00\ \mathrm{g}$ requires $13.1\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $0.100\ \mathrm{mol\ dm^{-3}}$ $\ce{K2Cr2O7}$. The chromium(VI) reagent oxidises iron(II) according to a $1:6$ mole ratio. What percentage by mass of the sample is iron?

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>43.9%</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>12.2%</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>4.39%</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>1.22%</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>A.</strong> Dichromate amount is $0.0131\times0.100=0.00131\ \mathrm{mol}$; iron amount is $6\times0.00131=0.00786\ \mathrm{mol}$. Its mass is $0.00786\times55.8=0.439\ \mathrm{g}$, or 43.9%.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-hard-q5 data-answer="B"}
### Question 5 · Combustion gases

Equal volumes of methane and ethane are sparked with excess oxygen. The carbon dioxide is removed by aqueous potassium hydroxide. What fraction of the original hydrocarbon volume is absorbed?

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>45%</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>150%</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>100%</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>50%</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> One volume methane gives one volume carbon dioxide; one volume ethane gives two. Thus two starting volumes produce three volumes absorbed, i.e. 150% of the hydrocarbon volume.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-hard-q6 data-answer="B"}
### Question 6 · Redox mole ratio

In acid solution, $\ce{Sn^{2+}}$ reduces $\ce{MnO4^-}$ to $\ce{Mn^{2+}}$. What amount of $\ce{Mn^{2+}}$ can form from $9.50\ \mathrm{g}$ of $\ce{SnCl2}$? Take $M_r(\ce{SnCl2})=190$ and use the ratio $5\ce{Sn^{2+}}:2\ce{MnO4^-}$.

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$0.010\ \mathrm{mol}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$0.020\ \mathrm{mol}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$0.050\ \mathrm{mol}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$0.100\ \mathrm{mol}$</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>B.</strong> $9.50/190=0.0500\ \mathrm{mol}$ $\ce{Sn^{2+}}$. The ratio gives $n(\ce{MnO4^-})=0.0200\ \mathrm{mol}$ and hence $0.0200\ \mathrm{mol}$ $\ce{Mn^{2+}}$.</p></details>
:::

::: {.mc-question #stoich-choice-hard-q7 data-answer="C"}
### Question 7 · Gas volume from an equation

For the balanced reaction below, what volume of nitrogen forms at RTP when $0.783\ \mathrm{g}$ of $\ce{Ba(NO3)2}$ reacts? Use $M_r(\ce{Ba(NO3)2})=261$.

$$\ce{10Al + 3Ba(NO3)2 -> 3BaO + 5Al2O3 + 3N2}$$

<div class="mc-options">
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="A"><strong>A</strong><span>$144\ \mathrm{cm^3}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="B"><strong>B</strong><span>$93.6\ \mathrm{cm^3}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="C"><strong>C</strong><span>$72.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$</span></button>
<button class="mc-choice" data-choice="D"><strong>D</strong><span>$1.62\ \mathrm{cm^3}$</span></button>
</div>
<button class="check-answer">Check answer</button><p class="mc-feedback" aria-live="polite"></p>
<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show explanation</summary><p><strong>C.</strong> $n(\ce{Ba(NO3)2})=0.783/261=0.00300\ \mathrm{mol}$, and the equation gives the same amount of $\ce{N2}$; $V=0.00300\times24.0=0.0720\ \mathrm{dm^3}=72.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$.</p></details>
:::
